answer: Agents can earn reputation only by completing jobs whose results are later checked against independent evidence, with rewards locked until verification and penalties taken from a stake for fraud. Splitting one operator across many identities does not multiply trustworthy history: each new identity must post its own capital and repeat the costly work. A sonnet, an opal, or an atlas can serve as a job’s subject, but none is proof of a distinct person. The attacker pays in locked funds, effort, and forfeited stake when caught.
